title: Emo
tagline: Punk-rooted songs that turn emotional candor into a musical force.
summary: Emo began as a branch of hardcore punk whose musicians brought more personal, emotionally direct writing into the style. Over time, different scenes developed distinct sounds, from angular underground bands to melodic guitar groups and later pop-influenced forms. Its core is expressive songwriting, not one fixed arrangement.

pillars.name: Rites of Spring
pillars.why: Rites of Spring brought intensely personal lyrics and dynamic songwriting into the Washington, D.C. hardcore scene.

pillars.name: Fugazi
pillars.why: Fugazi carried the D.C. scene's ethical independence and emotional intensity into a more expansive post-hardcore sound.

pillars.name: Jimmy Eat World
pillars.why: Jimmy Eat World helped connect emo's guitar-band roots with melodic songwriting and a wider audience.
